newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HKMA to manage Land Fund after handover - Tung.
newsitem.headline: HKMA to manage Land Fund after handover - Tung.

text.p: Hong Kong's future leader Tung Chee-hwa said on Wednesday the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) will manage the US$19 billion Land Fund after the British territory is handed back to China on July 1.
In a statement, Tung said Financial Secretary Donald Tsang will be responsible for management of the fund and chair a Land Fund committee to be set up on July 1.
"Initially, the Land Fund will be managed by the HKMA under the direction of the Financial Secretary," Tung said.
"The Financial Secretary will establish an advisory committee on July 1, 1997, to advise him on the investment strategy and management of the Land Fund."
HKMA chief executive Joseph Yam and Land Fund chief executive Chung Shui-ming will be vice-chairmen of the committee, the statement said.
Hong Kong reverts to Chinese rule at midnight on June 30 to become a Special Administrative Region (SAR) of China.

The arrangements will enable the future SAR government to consider and decide on the longer-term investment strategy for the fiscal reserves, of which the Land Fund forms a part, the statement from Tung's office said.
"This will not cause any unnecessary disruption to the existing arrangements for managing the Land Fund or the fiscal reserves in the Exchange Fund," it said.

The statement also said the existing investment strategy for the HK$150 billion (US$19 billion) Land Fund -- created in 1983 to hold half of the revenues from government land sales -- will remain "largely unchanged".
To ensure continuity of the management of the Land Fund, existing staff will be offered employment with the HKMA, it said.
Chung has indicated his intention not to join the HKMA and will cease his employment with the Trustees after the closing accounts of the Land Fund are submitted to Tung.
But the Land Fund is expected to benefit from Chung's new capacity as vice-chairman of the proposed committee, it added.
